title: A search for signatures of interactions of X-ray binary outflows with their environments with ALMA
question: Do five persistently accreting X-ray binaries (NS and BH, LMXB and HMXB) show atomic or molecular line emission from their accretion discs or from nearby sites of jet-ISM interaction, as seen with ALMA Band 3?

data.angular_resolution: Cir X-1 synthesised beam 0.67 x 0.63 arcsec (other sources in Table obslog2)
data.sensitivity: 3 sigma line limits of 0.65-3.7 K km/s at the XRB positions

what.value: Galactic YSO catalogue used to cross-match the SiO line position (source J181430.35-170901.0)

evidence.loc: Line emission in the field of view of GX 13+1
evidence.quote: We found a source coincident with the position of the line in the galactic young stellar object (YSO) catalogue of (cite: marton19cat)

what.value: Cir X-1 radio flare ephemeris used to derive the orbital phase of the ALMA observation

evidence.quote: Using the ephemeris in (cite: cirx1:nicolson07atel) derived from the onset times of 21 well-observed radio flares
GRS 1915+105 is a low-mass XRB (LMXB) at a distance of 8.6 kpc (cite: 1915:reid14apj)

what.value: Mass loss rate of W Hya used for the evolved-star comparison

evidence.loc: Line emission in the field of view of GX 13+1
evidence.quote: a mass loss rate of 4.9 $\times$ 10$^{-7}~M_\odot$ within a radius of about 70 AU has been derived (cite: vlemmings11apj)

recipe.method: Re-calibration with CASA and the integrated ALMA pipeline, then images regenerated from calibrated products with natural weighting
Phase-only self-calibration on the targets, except GX 13+1
assumptions: Phase decoherence attributed to poor phase rms conditions at low PWV

recipe.goal: measure continuum flux density and spectral index at each XRB
recipe.method: Peak flux of an elliptical Gaussian fitted in the image plane after primary beam correction; error is the image rms far from the source; spectral index between the two sidebands

recipe.goal: search the data cubes for line emission at the XRB positions
recipe.method: Data cubes extracted at the spectral resolution of the cubes and inspected for line emission; 3 sigma upper limits derived

recipe.goal: characterise line detections in the GX 13+1 field of view
recipe.method: Line emission found at three positions in the GX 13+1 field; peak intensities and frequencies tabulated

recipe.goal: identify the lines and constrain distances
recipe.method: Tentative SiO v=1 J=2-1 identification, with near and far kinematic distances computed from the velocity shift
assumptions: Line shift is due to position in the Galaxy, not intrinsic to the source

recipe.goal: test YSO versus evolved-star origin of the SiO line
recipe.method: Estimate expected continuum of a 1 solar-mass core and of an evolved star at 2.5 kpc and compare with ALMA limits; compare with YSO catalogue and archival surveys
assumptions: typically adopted dust opacity, gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100, optically thin emission at 90 GHz

recipe.goal: determine the accretion state at the time of observation
recipe.method: MAXI hardness-intensity and colour-colour diagrams classified following earlier work

evidence.quote: We detected significant continuum emission with a peak flux of 13.69 $\pm$ 0.05 mJy/beam
a spectral index of – 0.09 $\pm$ 0.01 between 84 and 99 GHz
The ALMA observations indicate a flux of 0.75 $\pm$ 0.02 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: we did not detect line emission at the position of any source down to 3 $\sigma$ limits of 0.65 –3.7 K km s$^{-1}$

score_reason: Project code, CASA version, weighting and self-calibration intervals are given and the headline numbers are simple, but cube imaging settings and line-limit methods are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from a 2016 ALMA project cited by code, the recipe (re-calibration, natural-weighted imaging, self-calibration solints, Gaussian peak fluxes) is mostly given, and results are numeric fluxes and limits.
